constraints._note: Creator constraints set at intake 2026-08-07. fin-facts and fin-audit both enforce these; they are not suggestions.
constraints.no_return_promise: Never promise or imply a return rate. The corpus number is arithmetic FROM a stated assumption, never a forecast. Say the assumption out loud in the VO the first time a number depends on it.
constraints.withdrawal_rate_on_screen: Every corpus figure must carry its assumed withdrawal/return rate ON SCREEN in the same frame as the number. A number without its assumption visible is a fabricated promise.
constraints.no_unsourced_retire_early: No 'retire early', 'quit your job', or financial-freedom-by-age claim that is not sourced and dated in facts-staging.md.
constraints.hi_currency_framing: ₹ cut: SIP/SWP vocabulary, financial freedom / passive income framing. The word 'dividend' (and its Hindi/Devanagari transliterations) must not appear in the hi script, on-screen text, title, or tags.
constraints.market_rewrite_not_translation: The en cut is a US rewrite (US vehicles, US numbers, Brian voice), not a translation of the hi cut — see vault/knowledge/us-english-script-style.md.
constraints.derived_income_carries_assumption: EXTENDED 2026-08-07 during ch2 review. `withdrawal_rate_on_screen` was written about CORPUS figures, so the build assert let s17's `WHAT ₹2,500 BUYS` through bare — correctly, by the letter. But ₹2,500/month is the corpus's OUTPUT at 3.0%, i.e. the promise the video actually makes, and `no_return_promise` says a number without its assumption visible is a fabricated promise. So a DERIVED INCOME figure carries the rate in frame or an explicit ILLUSTRATIVE marker, same as a corpus. Every rung has a 'what X buys' beat, so this lives in the build assert, not in per-chapter review.

style_decision._creator_2026-08-07: Use STYLE E for BOTH cuts. Start with the English one. English voice stays Brian. Hindi voice changes to Amrut Deshmukh LHJy3mhZWsvhUjy0zUM1.
style_decision.what_style_E_is: (1) The cold open is a WHAT-IF, not a statement — «सोचिए, एक ऐसा दिन…» / «Imagine a day when your phone does not ring once» — and the phone's silence is the promise while its single buzz is the payoff. (2) The teaching register is signposted throughout: «यहाँ ध्यान दीजिए» / «Notice this», «इसे ऐसे समझिए» / «Think of it this way», «Now watch what it buys», «Work it through». (3) An analogy that PAYS OFF LATER: the tank and the two taps — 'how much can you draw each year without emptying it' IS the safe-withdrawal question, so the later yield-trap beat becomes a callback rather than a new idea. (4) Arithmetic is stepped across lines, not compressed into one.
style_decision.reference_scripts: studio/voice-tests/passive-income-number/style-E-teacher-curiosity.txt (hi ch1-2) and style-E-en-teacher-curiosity.txt (en ch1-2). Both are ch1+ch2 only — chapters 3+ must be restyled to match, keeping their facts and structure unchanged.
style_decision.line_1_7_en_is_untouchable: «Everyone asks how much you need invested to live off dividends, and the honest answer costs more than the popular one.» It is the title's own promise and the phrase this format ranks on.

rate_key_en_followup: fin-voice measured 17.313 c/s flat on style E against 17.588 on the same voice reading the style-A draft — the key is ~1.5% optimistic for this register, because style E added an em-dash signpost to nine lines and stepped the arithmetic into shorter sentences, so more of each clip is pause. Same mechanic as the documented SHORT caveat. A four-cut mean would only move the key to 17.505, so 17.57 STANDS and fin-script carries a register note instead. The important signal is the shape: attempt 1 had all 78 lines drifting negative (a wrong key), this cut drifts two-sided (a roughly-correct one).
